full_judgment: 5. Mr. Moinul Hossain, the learned counsel for the appellant contended that on the solitary evidence of the complainant the appellant should not have been convicted in as much as, it was not at all safe to convict a person on the lone evidence of the vitally interested person, namely the complainant. He also drew our attention to some facts, namely that a cooly was carrying the cigarettes and was going with the complainant, that another shop keeper, namely Harunur Rashid who was also said to have been robbed of Tk. 10.25 was going with the complainant, that the cooly Md. Ali was examined but Harunur Rashid was not examined, that the cooly Md. Ali did not corroborate the complainant in material particulars and that the Special Tribunal, the Appellate Tribunal as well as the High Court Division did not consider this aspect of the case. Obviously, this is a question of fact. This Court is not intended to go into consideration of the: facts with reference to the evidence; It appears that the High Court Division found that there was an occurrence as alleged by the complainant. It also appears that the 'Special Tribunal as well as the Appellate Tribunal noticed that some persons who ought to have been examined were not examined, still no adverse presumption was drawn by the Tribunal as well as by the High Court Division as provided under illustration (g) of section 114 of the Evidence Act. Rather the Special Tribunal as well as the Appellate Tribunal believed the occurrence and relied on the solitary evidence of the complainant. The High Court Division declined to' interfere on an extra-ordinary Writ of Certiorari in view of the fact that the Special Tribunal as well as the Appellate Tribunal found the occurrence to be true.
